facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: For ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC the filed statements support a clear financial base through Q3 2026, with the limits stated here. On the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, last twelve months leverage on gross debt fell from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at Q3 2026 and net leverage from 5.73x to 4.94x, because last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA grew from 676,958 to 831,829 (US$ thousands) while principal debt rose from 4,033,394 to 4,267,981. Cash interest cover on the same basis rose from 2.61x to 3.07x. Liquidity narrowed: the issuer-stated availability under the Global Senior Facility moved from 814.3 US$m at FY2025 to 510.2 US$m at Q3 2026 as the revolver funded the settlement of the 2029 convertible notes, and the other two debt facilities are fully drawn. The maturity profile is long: the notes tables show no instrument maturing before 2028, and the largest single maturity year is 2029 (the revolver and the U.S. Facility). The measure itself carries definition risk: roughly two fifths of nine month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is revenue from changes in recoveries that the cash flow statement deducts as non-cash, and the large purchases of receivable portfolios needed to sustain collections sit in investing cash flow, outside both Adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow. Covenant headroom is not measurable because only limits and a compliance statement are printed. Overall this is a usable base for leverage, coverage and liquidity work, with Medium confidence on the headline ratios.

facts.label: Definition review
facts.text: - Adjusted EBITDA is defined by the company as net income before interest income and expense, taxes, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, acquisition, integration and restructuring expenses and other non-recurring charges or gains (Q1 10-Q page:39, "Adjusted EBITDA. Management utilizes adjusted EBITDA (defined as net income before interest income and expense, taxes, depreciation and amortization"). It is a management measure, not a covenant measure; the covenant definitions are in executed agreements that are not supplied. - Revenue inside Adjusted EBITDA includes changes in recoveries, which the cash flow statement removes as non-cash (Q3 10-Q page:3 "Changes in recoveries 111,043 63,636 244,898 140,699" and the cash flow adjustment on Q3 10-Q page:5). Nine month 2026 changes in recoveries of 244,898 are 38.0% of nine month Adjusted EBITDA of 644,320 (calculated). Forecast-driven revenue makes the measure more sensitive to collection forecast changes than a cash measure. - Portfolio purchases are the core reinvestment of the business and are in investing cash flow, outside both Adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow: nine month 2026 purchases of 1,187,072 compare with Adjusted EBITDA of 644,320 and operating cash flow of 159,630. Debt to Adjusted EBITDA therefore does not measure the cash left for debt service after reinvestment. - Total debt here is principal before discount and costs, including finance leases, and includes consolidated securitisation debt of the Cabot vehicle and the U.S. subsidiary that is secured on its own assets; the balance sheet VIE table shows borrowings of 784,567 thousand (Q3 10-Q page:3). The restricted group perimeter's own debt, EBITDA and covenant ratios are not printed. - Operating lease liabilities are not in total debt (operating lease right-of-use assets are in other assets, Q3 10-Q page:18). The undiscounted operating lease payments at FY2025 were 73,761 thousand (10-K page:71). Forward flow purchase commitments of 684.5 US$m minimum are outside debt (Q3 10-Q page:30). - Foreign currency: sterling and euro instruments are translated at period-end rates (for example Q3 10-Q page:25, "approximately $338.2 million based on an exchange rate of $1.00 to £0.75"), so reported US$ debt moves with exchange rates. The EBITDA is in US$ after translation of European results.

facts.label: Evidence, risk mechanism and credit implication
facts.text: - Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA last twelve months to Q3 2026 of 831,829 against principal debt of 4,267,981. Risk mechanism: the measure includes forecast-driven revenue and excludes the reinvestment spend that the model needs to replace runoff. Credit implication: the improvement in headline leverage is real on the filed numbers but overstates cash coverage; debt capacity should also be tested against collections and ERC. - Evidence: revolver availability of 510.2 US$m at Q3 2026 against 814.3 US$m at FY2025, and all other facilities fully drawn. Risk mechanism: future portfolio purchases and refinancing are funded from the revolver, whose availability is covenant-limited and expires in 2029 (2028 for one tranche). Credit implication: liquidity headroom is thinner than a year ago, though no debt matures before 2028 in the notes tables. - Evidence: a long list of senior secured instruments sharing collateral with a super senior revolver. Risk mechanism: enforcement proceeds on shared collateral go first to the revolver and super senior hedging. Credit implication: recovery for the senior secured notes depends on the revolver balance at default, which has risen.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: For ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC the business is a consumer debt purchaser and collector that buys charged-off receivables at deep discounts, collects through call centers, digital channels and legal action, and recognises revenue from portfolio yield plus forecast-driven changes in recoveries. The United States business (MCM) is the dominant revenue and purchasing engine and Europe (Cabot, with the United Kingdom, France and Spain) is smaller and growing more slowly, with competitive pricing limiting European deployment. The company is a widely held listed company with no sponsor or controlling owner named in the sources, which removes sponsor extraction and sponsor support as drivers but leaves shareholder returns, funded in part from the revolver, as the capital allocation question. There is no live acquisition or sponsor transaction. The transaction record is a sequence of refinancings in 2025 and 2026 that extended the senior secured note maturities to 2031 to 2033 for the new issues, replaced a high coupon note, and, in the third quarter of 2026, retired the convertible notes in cash from revolver drawings; the effect on liquidity and leverage is in the financial base handoff. Credit-relevant business risks are forecast and pricing risk in a business where revenue recognition depends on collection forecasts, regulatory and litigation exposure that is continuing but not reserved, supply concentration among a few large sellers whose shares are not disclosed, and a heavy reliance on forward flow agreements that can be repriced or terminated. The view is Medium confidence because ownership, seller concentration and the executed financing terms are not in the sources.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no sponsor transaction, merger, disposal or leveraged recapitalisation in the sources; the transaction record is financing activity only, and each item is completed unless stated. In the fourth quarter of 2025 the company issued 500.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due April 2031 at an issue price of 100.000% and used a portion of proceeds to pay down revolver drawings (10-K page:69 "we issued $500.0 million 6.625% in senior secured notes that mature in 2031"); settled its 100.0 US$m 2025 convertible notes in cash for 106.2 US$m using revolver borrowings (10-K page:109 "In October 2025, the Company settled its $100.0 million 2025 Convertible Notes"); and repaid 100.0 EUR m of the 2028 Floating Rate Notes with revolver borrowings in November 2025 (10-K page:70). In 2026, on 2026-05-22 the company issued 750.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due June 2032 at 100.000% and used proceeds to redeem in full the 500.0 US$m 9.250% notes due 2029, with a loss on extinguishment of 28.0 US$m including a 23.1 US$m make-whole premium (Q3 10-Q page:22 "Encore 2032 Notes"). On 2026-05-28 it issued 325.0 EUR m of floating rate notes due July 2033 at three-month EURIBOR plus 3.250% and, with revolver drawings, redeemed the 415.0 EUR m 2028 Floating Rate Notes, with a loss on extinguishment of 2.5 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:22). The nine month loss on extinguishment of 30,533 thousand is the sum of these two items and was booked in Q2 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:3). Management said the Q2 result absorbed 1.00 US$ per share of refinancing costs (Q2 release page:1 "includes $1.00 per share of refinancing costs"), which is management language. On 2026-07-22 the company called its 230.0 US$m 4.000% convertible notes due 2029 and on 2026-09-24 settled them in cash for 367.9 US$m funded by revolver borrowings, unwinding the capped call hedges for 31.8 US$m of proceeds; the 137.9 US$m excess over principal was charged to equity (Q3 10-Q page:24). On 2026-08-17 the U.S. Facility was extended from October 2028 to October 2029 and its margin reduced from 3.50% to 3.00% (Q3 10-Q page:25). In October 2026, after the balance sheet date and before the cutoff, new interest rate swaps with 150.0 US$m notional replaced swaps that matured on 2026-10-27 (Q3 10-Q page:14). The use of proceeds was refinancing in every case; the effect on liquidity and leverage is that debt rose over 2026 and revolver availability fell to 510.2 US$m at 2026-09-30 (financial base handoff). In the equity-side actions, the company repurchased 73.4 US$m of stock in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (Q3 10-Q page:58), expected to be funded from cash and revolver drawings. The company has not announced a pending transaction in the sources read, and the only acquisition-type event in the sources is the December 2024 step-up acquisition of EARC, with 11.3 US$m of goodwill recognised (10-K page:128).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability: Evidence: revenue is dominated by debt purchasing revenue, of which changes in recoveries are a non-cash forecast component (Q3 10-Q page:3; Q3 10-Q page:18). Risk mechanic: revenue and Adjusted EBITDA are sensitive to collection forecast revisions, and recent vintages have been revised up after sustained over-performance. Implication: earnings improvement is real on filed numbers but carries forecast reversal risk; monitoring should track recoveries above forecast and ERC (financial base handoff). A counter-consideration is that management concluded the over-performance did not represent a material shift in timing. - Margin and cash flow risk: Evidence: cost of legal collections up 25.7% for nine months on increased US legal placements (Q3 10-Q page:47). Risk mechanic: legal-channel collections carry court and fee costs and conduct risk. Implication: margin gains depend on the legal channel remaining productive; operating cash flow is small relative to Adjusted EBITDA because purchases are in investing cash flow (financial base handoff). - Concentration risk: Evidence: purchases may be concentrated with a few large sellers (10-K page:98), with no shares disclosed. Risk mechanic: a seller exit would cut supply and pricing leverage. Implication: Insufficient Information; seller shares are a priority monitoring datapoint. - Sponsor alignment: Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is named (10-K page:45). Risk mechanic: no sponsor support to cure a liquidity shortfall and no sponsor extraction. Implication: creditors rely on internal cash generation and market access; the repeated 2025 and 2026 refinancings show access but are not a commitment. - Key uncertainties: executed covenant terms, seller concentration, large holders, target leverage and ratings, all not supplied.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Encore Capital Group's credit profile is improving but still highly levered: earnings and collections have grown faster than debt through 2026, yet the company remains a refinancing-dependent debt purchaser. The strongest support is last twelve months leverage of 5.13x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, down from 5.96x at FY2025, with cash interest cover of 3.07x, no scheduled maturity before 2028 in the notes tables and a long-dated senior secured note stack. The weakest point is earnings quality and liquidity: Adjusted EBITDA includes forecast-driven revenue, portfolio purchases sit outside it, and revolver availability fell to USD 510.2 million after the convertible notes were settled in cash. What decides the outcome is whether collections keep beating forecasts and whether the revolver is rebuilt rather than drawn further. [CP-1] [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Leverage fell on the company's own measure while debt rose. Evidence: total debt to Adjusted EBITDA moved from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at Q3 2026 on a last twelve months basis, with principal debt rising from USD 4,033,394 thousand to USD 4,267,981 thousand and last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA rising from USD 676,958 thousand to USD 831,829 thousand [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: the gain comes from earnings growth, not from debt reduction. Credit implication: leverage is falling because collections are strong; it would rise again if earnings fell, since debt is not being repaid. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Debt rose over 2026 but earnings grew faster: total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at the last twelve months to Q3 2026, while revolver availability fell to 510.2 US$m. | Medium | The earnings measure is the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, and no covenant ratios or executed agreements are available. |

| Adjusted EBITDA includes forecast-driven revenue that is deducted as non-cash in operating cash flow, and portfolio purchases sit outside it. | Headline leverage overstates cash earnings capacity available for debt service. | High |

### Financial base view

For ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC the filed statements support a clear financial base through Q3 2026, with the limits stated here. On the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, last twelve months leverage on gross debt fell from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at Q3 2026 and net leverage from 5.73x to 4.94x, because last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA grew from 676,958 to 831,829 (US$ thousands) while principal debt rose from 4,033,394 to 4,267,981. Cash interest cover on the same basis rose from 2.61x to 3.07x. Liquidity narrowed: the issuer-stated availability under the Global Senior Facility moved from 814.3 US$m at FY2025 to 510.2 US$m at Q3 2026 as the revolver funded the settlement of the 2029 convertible notes, and the other two debt facilities are fully drawn. The maturity profile is long: the notes tables show no instrument maturing before 2028, and the largest single maturity year is 2029 (the revolver and the U.S. Facility). The measure itself carries definition risk: roughly two fifths of nine month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA is revenue from changes in recoveries that the cash flow statement deducts as non-cash, and the large purchases of receivable portfolios needed to sustain collections sit in investing cash flow, outside both Adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow. Covenant headroom is not measurable because only limits and a compliance statement are printed. Overall this is a usable base for leverage, coverage and liquidity work, with Medium confidence on the headline ratios.

### Definition review

- Adjusted EBITDA is defined by the company as net income before interest income and expense, taxes, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, acquisition, integration and restructuring expenses and other non-recurring charges or gains (Q1 10-Q page:39, "Adjusted EBITDA. Management utilizes adjusted EBITDA (defined as net income before interest income and expense, taxes, depreciation and amortization"). It is a management measure, not a covenant measure; the covenant definitions are in executed agreements that are not supplied.

- Revenue inside Adjusted EBITDA includes changes in recoveries, which the cash flow statement removes as non-cash (Q3 10-Q page:3 "Changes in recoveries 111,043 63,636 244,898 140,699" and the cash flow adjustment on Q3 10-Q page:5). Nine month 2026 changes in recoveries of 244,898 are 38.0% of nine month Adjusted EBITDA of 644,320 (calculated). Forecast-driven revenue makes the measure more sensitive to collection forecast changes than a cash measure.

- Portfolio purchases are the core reinvestment of the business and are in investing cash flow, outside both Adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow: nine month 2026 purchases of 1,187,072 compare with Adjusted EBITDA of 644,320 and operating cash flow of 159,630. Debt to Adjusted EBITDA therefore does not measure the cash left for debt service after reinvestment.

- Total debt here is principal before discount and costs, including finance leases, and includes consolidated securitisation debt of the Cabot vehicle and the U.S. subsidiary that is secured on its own assets; the balance sheet VIE table shows borrowings of 784,567 thousand (Q3 10-Q page:3). The restricted group perimeter's own debt, EBITDA and covenant ratios are not printed.

- Operating lease liabilities are not in total debt (operating lease right-of-use assets are in other assets, Q3 10-Q page:18). The undiscounted operating lease payments at FY2025 were 73,761 thousand (10-K page:71). Forward flow purchase commitments of 684.5 US$m minimum are outside debt (Q3 10-Q page:30).

- Foreign currency: sterling and euro instruments are translated at period-end rates (for example Q3 10-Q page:25, "approximately $338.2 million based on an exchange rate of $1.00 to £0.75"), so reported US$ debt moves with exchange rates. The EBITDA is in US$ after translation of European results.
### Cash flow and liquidity read

- Operating cash flow is small relative to Adjusted EBITDA and volatile by quarter. The sum of operating and investing cash flow was a deficit of 16,008 for nine months 2026 against a deficit of 79,161 for nine months 2025 (calculated), so the business consumed cash before financing in both periods while growing the portfolio balance.

- The revolver funded the 2026 refinancing and the convertible settlement. Drawings on the Global Senior Facility rose from 691,648 at Q2 2026 to 974,763 at Q3 2026, an increase of 283,115 (calculated), after the 2029 convertible notes were settled in cash for 367.9 US$m, partly offset by 31.8 US$m of capped call proceeds (Q3 10-Q page:24). Utilisation of the 1,485.0 US$m commitment was 65.6% at Q3 2026 against 42.6% at FY2025 (calculated); the loan to value covenant of 0.75 applies when utilisation exceeds 20% (Q3 10-Q page:20), so that covenant is live in every period shown.
- Fixed charge coverage covenant: at least 2.0 (Q3 10-Q page:20). The issuer's definition and reported ratio are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable.

- Share repurchases are also financed from the revolver or cash: nine months 2026 repurchases were 73,993 in the cash flow statement (Q3 10-Q page:5 financing section), with remaining authority of 229.0 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:58).
### Refinancing events and subsequent events to the cutoff

- 2026-05-22: issued 750.0 US$m 6.625% Encore 2032 Notes at 100.000%, used to redeem the 500.0 US$m 9.250% Encore 2029 Notes; loss on extinguishment 28.0 US$m including a 23.1 US$m make-whole premium (Q3 10-Q page:22).

- 2026-05-28: issued 325.0 EUR m Encore 2033 Floating Rate Notes and redeemed the 415.0 EUR m Encore 2028 Floating Rate Notes using the proceeds and revolver drawings; loss on extinguishment 2.5 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:22). Total loss on extinguishment for nine months 2026 is 30,533 thousand (Q3 10-Q page:3), booked in Q2 2026.

- 2026-07-22 and 2026-09-24: called and settled the 2029 convertible notes in cash for 367.9 US$m; the 137.9 US$m excess over principal was charged to equity, not to the income statement (Q3 10-Q page:24).
- 2026-08-17: U.S. Facility amended, maturity extended from October 2028 to October 2029 and margin reduced from 3.50% to 3.00% (Q3 10-Q page:25).
- October 2026 (after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet date, before the cutoff): new interest rate swaps with 150.0 US$m notional replaced swaps that matured on 2026-10-27 (Q3 10-Q page:14).
- 2026-11-04: Q3 results and raised full-year 2026 guidance (Q3 release page:1), management forward-looking statement, not evidence of outcome.
### Evidence, risk mechanism and credit implication

- Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA last twelve months to Q3 2026 of 831,829 against principal debt of 4,267,981. Risk mechanism: the measure includes forecast-driven revenue and excludes the reinvestment spend that the model needs to replace runoff. Credit implication: the improvement in headline leverage is real on the filed numbers but overstates cash coverage; debt capacity should also be tested against collections and ERC.

- Evidence: revolver availability of 510.2 US$m at Q3 2026 against 814.3 US$m at FY2025, and all other facilities fully drawn. Risk mechanism: future portfolio purchases and refinancing are funded from the revolver, whose availability is covenant-limited and expires in 2029 (2028 for one tranche). Credit implication: liquidity headroom is thinner than a year ago, though no debt matures before 2028 in the notes tables.

- Evidence: a long list of senior secured instruments sharing collateral with a super senior revolver. Risk mechanism: enforcement proceeds on shared collateral go first to the revolver and super senior hedging. Credit implication: recovery for the senior secured notes depends on the revolver balance at default, which has risen.
## Calculations
All inputs are US$ thousands as printed unless stated; each result is computed from the figures cited above.
8. Share of nine month Adjusted EBITDA from changes in recoveries: 244,898 / 644,320 = 38.0%.
9. Operating plus investing cash flow: nine months 2026 159,630 + (175,638) = (16,008); nine months 2025 136,388 + (215,549) = (79,161).

10. Revolver: commitment less drawn at Q3 2026: 1,485.0 − 974.763 = 510.237, agreeing with the stated 510.2 US$m. At Q2: 1,485.0 − 691.648 = 793.352 against stated 793.4. At Q1: 1,485.0 − 681.267 = 803.733 against stated 791.3 (difference 12.4). At FY2025: 1,485.0 − 631.998 = 853.002 against stated 814.3 (difference 38.7). Utilisation: 974.763 / 1,485.0 = 65.6% at Q3 2026; 631.998 / 1,485.0 = 42.6% at FY2025. Drawing increase Q2 to Q3: 974,763 − 691,648 = 283,115.

12. Consistency of year-end 2025 debt across filings: total principal 4,033,394 and carrying 4,001,293 are the same in the 10-K and in the Q1, Q2 and Q3 10-Q comparatives. Difference between principal and carrying at Q3: 4,267,981 − 4,237,800 = 30,181, equal to the printed discount and costs.

Pass the following forward to the business and transaction fact pack and the credit synthesis. ### Business and transaction view

For ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC the business is a consumer debt purchaser and collector that buys charged-off receivables at deep discounts, collects through call centers, digital channels and legal action, and recognises revenue from portfolio yield plus forecast-driven changes in recoveries. The United States business (MCM) is the dominant revenue and purchasing engine and Europe (Cabot, with the United Kingdom, France and Spain) is smaller and growing more slowly, with competitive pricing limiting European deployment. The company is a widely held listed company with no sponsor or controlling owner named in the sources, which removes sponsor extraction and sponsor support as drivers but leaves shareholder returns, funded in part from the revolver, as the capital allocation question. There is no live acquisition or sponsor transaction. The transaction record is a sequence of refinancings in 2025 and 2026 that extended the senior secured note maturities to 2031 to 2033 for the new issues, replaced a high coupon note, and, in the third quarter of 2026, retired the convertible notes in cash from revolver drawings; the effect on liquidity and leverage is in the financial base handoff. Credit-relevant business risks are forecast and pricing risk in a business where revenue recognition depends on collection forecasts, regulatory and litigation exposure that is continuing but not reserved, supply concentration among a few large sellers whose shares are not disclosed, and a heavy reliance on forward flow agreements that can be repriced or terminated. The view is Medium confidence because ownership, seller concentration and the executed financing terms are not in the sources.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

There is no sponsor transaction, merger, disposal or leveraged recapitalisation in the sources; the transaction record is financing activity only, and each item is completed unless stated. In the fourth quarter of 2025 the company issued 500.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due April 2031 at an issue price of 100.000% and used a portion of proceeds to pay down revolver drawings (10-K page:69 "we issued $500.0 million 6.625% in senior secured notes that mature in 2031"); settled its 100.0 US$m 2025 convertible notes in cash for 106.2 US$m using revolver borrowings (10-K page:109 "In October 2025, the Company settled its $100.0 million 2025 Convertible Notes"); and repaid 100.0 EUR m of the 2028 Floating Rate Notes with revolver borrowings in November 2025 (10-K page:70). In 2026, on 2026-05-22 the company issued 750.0 US$m of 6.625% Senior Secured Notes due June 2032 at 100.000% and used proceeds to redeem in full the 500.0 US$m 9.250% notes due 2029, with a loss on extinguishment of 28.0 US$m including a 23.1 US$m make-whole premium (Q3 10-Q page:22 "Encore 2032 Notes"). On 2026-05-28 it issued 325.0 EUR m of floating rate notes due July 2033 at three-month EURIBOR plus 3.250% and, with revolver drawings, redeemed the 415.0 EUR m 2028 Floating Rate Notes, with a loss on extinguishment of 2.5 US$m (Q3 10-Q page:22). The nine month loss on extinguishment of 30,533 thousand is the sum of these two items and was booked in Q2 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:3). Management said the Q2 result absorbed 1.00 US$ per share of refinancing costs (Q2 release page:1 "includes $1.00 per share of refinancing costs"), which is management language. On 2026-07-22 the company called its 230.0 US$m 4.000% convertible notes due 2029 and on 2026-09-24 settled them in cash for 367.9 US$m funded by revolver borrowings, unwinding the capped call hedges for 31.8 US$m of proceeds; the 137.9 US$m excess over principal was charged to equity (Q3 10-Q page:24). On 2026-08-17 the U.S. Facility was extended from October 2028 to October 2029 and its margin reduced from 3.50% to 3.00% (Q3 10-Q page:25). In October 2026, after the balance sheet date and before the cutoff, new interest rate swaps with 150.0 US$m notional replaced swaps that matured on 2026-10-27 (Q3 10-Q page:14). The use of proceeds was refinancing in every case; the effect on liquidity and leverage is that debt rose over 2026 and revolver availability fell to 510.2 US$m at 2026-09-30 (financial base handoff). In the equity-side actions, the company repurchased 73.4 US$m of stock in the nine months to 2026-09-30 (Q3 10-Q page:58), expected to be funded from cash and revolver drawings. The company has not announced a pending transaction in the sources read, and the only acquisition-type event in the sources is the December 2024 step-up acquisition of EARC, with 11.3 US$m of goodwill recognised (10-K page:128).

- Sponsor alignment: Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is named (10-K page:45). Risk mechanic: no sponsor support to cure a liquidity shortfall and no sponsor extraction. spans.text: ## Request

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for ENCORE CAPITAL GROUP INC as of 2026-11-05 on the credit_snapshot pathway, with a cutoff of 2026-11-05 and USD as the reporting currency. It combines the business view and the financial base from the upstream handoffs only, and reads no source text of its own. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs
This module quotes no source text. The seven issuer sources below were read by the upstream modules, and every figure here is a reference to those handoffs.
| Source name | sha256 |
| EX-99.1_2026-08-05_exhibit991ecpgq22026earnin.htm.jsonl | c912421ecebbdeab115865e4c75e4397e60fc06977b32c09b5fe72e8026c1bc7 |
| EX-99.1_2026-11-04_exhibit991ecpgq32026earnin.htm.jsonl | 55d38b7d96066eb32a5cc33bf9d08102e9a0e050298f0028532e13cfed8c82ea |
The context file (sha256 fb9232dcd1631add7bbcdb6eec1a7bd4a0eec6466deb6a3148ebd7ee287099b7) holds run settings only and is not issuer evidence.
### Handoffs
| Module | sha256 | Role |
| CP-0 | 5bceebdd4466b332506213f28eb141aebd7b80ad1c46615c0f3d948e9eb94d38 | Source readiness: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, with the gaps it lists |
| CP-1 | ab3610ee01f0fa09c54f50e64a0bffd5255ff6bf09c099588a370bee5b40463a | Financial base: leverage, interest cover, liquidity, maturities, definitions, refinancing sequence |
| CP-1A | 5dbcb538d13bbcbc9dec75ccc4fa14160823a451153ddae0cc3fd648d434d139 | Business and transaction view: operating model, profile, governance behaviour, timeline |
In this handoff, [CP-1] means the financial base handoff and [CP-1A: row] means a named row of the business view handoff; the row names used are the area or item names in its tables.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Encore is an improving but still highly levered debt purchaser: leverage fell to 5.13x and cash interest cover rose to 3.07x, but revolver availability narrowed to USD 510.2 million and earnings quality depends on collection forecasts. | Medium | Covenant ratios, seller concentration, ratings and executed financing terms are not available. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x on a last twelve months basis at Q3 2026. | Debt service capacity improved on the company-defined earnings measure. | Medium |

| Revolver availability fell from USD 814.3 million to USD 510.2 million after the convertible notes were settled from revolver drawings. | Less undrawn liquidity to fund purchases and refinancing. | High |
| Adjusted EBITDA includes forecast-driven revenue and excludes portfolio purchases. | Headline leverage overstates cash earnings capacity for debt service. | High |
| No debt matures before 2028 in the notes tables, and the largest maturity year is 2029. | Refinancing pressure is back-ended but concentrated on the revolver and the U.S. facility. | High |
| Covenant headroom, seller concentration and large shareholders are not measurable from the sources. | These items are monitoring gaps, not adverse findings. | Medium |
### Credit view

Encore Capital Group's credit profile is improving but still highly levered: earnings and collections have grown faster than debt through 2026, yet the company remains a refinancing-dependent debt purchaser. The strongest support is last twelve months leverage of 5.13x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, down from 5.96x at FY2025, with cash interest cover of 3.07x, no scheduled maturity before 2028 in the notes tables and a long-dated senior secured note stack. The weakest point is earnings quality and liquidity: Adjusted EBITDA includes forecast-driven revenue, portfolio purchases sit outside it, and revolver availability fell to USD 510.2 million after the convertible notes were settled in cash. What decides the outcome is whether collections keep beating forecasts and whether the revolver is rebuilt rather than drawn further. [CP-1] [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]
### Assessment and thesis
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Improving profile with high but falling leverage, adequate cash interest cover, long note maturities, and narrower revolver headroom; business risk is driven by purchase pricing, collection forecasts and legal-channel conduct. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | [CP-1] leverage, interest cover, liquidity and maturity series; [CP-1A: Core activity], [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk], [CP-1A: Collection channels, nine months 2026] |

| Thesis | Encore's debt service rests on continued collection over-performance and revolver access, which together support falling leverage today but leave limited cushion if forecasts reverse. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | [CP-1] Adjusted EBITDA and liquidity; [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk] |

Confidence is below High because the readiness handoff records no executed agreements, no ratings and no reported covenant ratios, and the business view records seller concentration, ownership and target leverage as Insufficient Information.
### Key findings

1. Leverage fell on the company's own measure while debt rose. Evidence: total debt to Adjusted EBITDA moved from 5.96x at FY2025 to 5.13x at Q3 2026 on a last twelve months basis, with principal debt rising from USD 4,033,394 thousand to USD 4,267,981 thousand and last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA rising from USD 676,958 thousand to USD 831,829 thousand [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: the gain comes from earnings growth, not from debt reduction. Credit implication: leverage is falling because collections are strong; it would rise again if earnings fell, since debt is not being repaid. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading.

2. Cash interest cover improved and is adequate on a last twelve months basis. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA over cash paid for interest was 3.07x at Q3 2026 against 2.61x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: cash interest is paid on semi-annual coupon dates, so single quarters mislead and the last twelve months basis is the right one. Credit implication: debt service is covered more than three times on the company measure, but the measure is before the portfolio purchases that sustain collections. Category: Documentary Fact.

3. Revolver headroom narrowed after the convertible settlement. Evidence: issuer-stated availability under the Global Senior Facility moved from USD 814.3 million at FY2025 to USD 510.2 million at Q3 2026, the revolver draw rose from USD 691,648 thousand at Q2 2026 to USD 974,763 thousand at Q3 2026, and utilisation was 65.6% against 42.6% at FY2025; the other facilities are drawn to their commitments [CP-1]. Risk mechanic: purchases, refinancing and share repurchases are all funded from the revolver, and the loan to value covenant applies once utilisation exceeds 20%, so it is live. Credit implication: liquidity is thinner than a year ago and covenant headroom cannot be measured. Category: Documentary Fact; the covenant gap is Insufficient Information.

4. Adjusted EBITDA quality is the central definition risk. Evidence: nine month 2026 changes in recoveries of USD 244,898 thousand are 38.0% of nine month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 644,320 thousand, and are deducted as non-cash in operating cash flow of USD 159,630 thousand, while purchases of USD 1,187,072 thousand sit in investing cash flow [CP-1]; management concluded over-performance did not represent a material shift in timing, which is Management Language [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]. Risk mechanic: revenue depends on forecast revisions that can reverse. Credit implication: headline leverage and cover overstate the cash left for debt service after reinvestment. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

5. The maturity profile is long but concentrated in 2029. Evidence: no instrument in the notes tables matures before 2028, USD 331.6 million of sterling notes matures in 2028, and USD 1424.8 million (the revolver and the U.S. facility) matures in 2029 [CP-1]; the 2026 refinancings replaced the 9.250% 2029 notes with 6.625% 2032 notes and extended the U.S. facility to October 2029 [CP-1A: Transaction summary]. Risk mechanic: the largest refinancing step is the secured bank-style funding that also supports daily purchasing. Credit implication: refinancing risk is back-ended but a single event, the 2029 renewal of both the revolver and the U.S. facility, matters. Category: Documentary Fact.

6. Business risk centres on pricing, forecasts and the legal channel. Evidence: the business is dominated by debt purchasing revenue, United States purchasing is funded largely by forward flow agreements with a minimum commitment of USD 684.5 million, cost of legal collections rose 25.7% for nine months 2026 on higher US legal placements, and no material legal reserves are recorded [CP-1A: Revenue streams, Q3 2026], [CP-1A: Forward flow commitments], [CP-1A: Cost structure]. Risk mechanic: pricing and forecast errors flow into revenue; legal collections carry court cost and conduct risk. Credit implication: earnings are sensitive to collection performance and regulation, and seller concentration is Insufficient Information. Category: Documentary Fact; seller concentration is Insufficient Information.

7. Governance gives creditors no sponsor support and no sponsor extraction. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder is named, there is no dividend history, share repurchases of USD 89.5 million in 2025 and USD 73.4 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 are expected to be funded partly from the revolver, and the refinancing record is repeated [CP-1A: Ownership and control], [CP-1A: Distributions]. Risk mechanic: shareholder returns compete with deleveraging for revolver capacity. Credit implication: capital allocation is a monitoring point; behaviour is Neutral or Mixed on documented actions only. Category: Documentary Fact for the actions, Analyst Interpretation for the behaviour label.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Earnings momentum: last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 831,829 thousand and collections and portfolio balances grew [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (2) Long-dated secured note stack with a lower coupon after the 2026 refinancings and no scheduled maturity before 2028 in the notes tables [CP-1] [CP-1A: Transaction summary]; Documentary Fact. (3) Demonstrated market access through repeated 2025 and 2026 issuance and a revolver maturing in 2029 [CP-1] [CP-1A: Timeline]; Documentary Fact, with the implication a reading of the record, so Analyst Interpretation. (4) Cash interest cover of 3.07x on a last twelve months basis [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (5) Large US purchasing platform with a forward flow base that provides purchase visibility, with a minimum commitment of USD 684.5 million [CP-1A: Forward flow commitments]; Documentary Fact. Management's statements that competitive scale favors larger participants are carried as Management Language and not adopted [CP-1A: Competition].

Weaknesses. (1) Leverage remains high at 5.13x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA and 4.94x net [CP-1]; Documentary Fact. (2) Earnings quality: forecast-driven revenue inside Adjusted EBITDA and purchases outside it [CP-1] [CP-1A: Revenue recognition and forecast risk]; Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. (3) Narrower revolver headroom of USD 510.2 million, a revolver that funds purchases, refinancing and repurchases, and a revolver ranking ahead of the notes on shared collateral enforcement [CP-1]; Documentary Fact, with the ranking a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion. (4) Legal-channel dependence and continuing regulatory exposure, including state Attorney General discussions [CP-1A: Legal and regulatory], [CP-1A: Collection channels, nine months 2026]; Documentary Fact. (5) Unmeasurable items: covenant headroom, seller concentration, large holders, target leverage and ratings [CP-0] [CP-1A: Concentration of sellers]; Insufficient Information, stated as gaps and not as adverse conclusions.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Collection forecast reversal | Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA include forecast-driven changes in recoveries; recent vintages were revised up after over-performance. | Revenue and leverage deteriorate together if collections fall back; debt does not fall with revenue. | Material |

| Revolver dependence and covenant limit | The revolver funds purchases, refinancing and repurchases; availability is stated after covenants, and the loan to value covenant is live above 20% utilisation. | Less capacity to absorb a weak quarter; headroom unmeasured. | Material |
| 2029 refinancing concentration | The revolver and the U.S. facility both mature in 2029. | A single renewal event; failure would affect both purchasing capacity and the secured stack. | Material |

| Legal and conduct exposure | Heavy use of the legal channel and ongoing state Attorney General discussions. | Potential penalties, new operating requirements or changes in collection practice. | Material |

| Seller concentration | Purchases may be concentrated with a few sellers; shares not disclosed. | Insufficient Information; supply loss would cut volume and pricing leverage. | Material (monitoring) |

| Foreign exchange and rate exposure | Sterling and euro debt is translated at period-end rates and floating-rate notes and facilities are used with interest rate hedges. | Reported US dollar debt and interest move with rates and currency. | Minor |
## Calculations

No new calculation. Every figure is a reference to a figure already shown, with its inputs, in the financial base handoff, or to a figure printed in the business view handoff. No ratio is derived here; the comparison of 5.13x with 5.96x, of 3.07x with 2.61x, and of USD 510.2 million with USD 814.3 million is a direction read from the two printed values.
## Gaps

| Letters of credit or ancillary usage under the revolver not supplied; the difference between commitment less drawn and stated availability at FY2025 and Q1 2026 is unexplained. | The true liquidity cushion at those dates is uncertain. | Liquidity | Minor | Obtain facility utilisation detail. |

| Beneficial ownership and related-party transactions not supplied (proxy not in the pack). | Control and related-party leakage cannot be assessed. | Governance | Minor | Supply the proxy statement. |

Proceed to the evidence trace review (CP-5). It should check that each figure in this handoff matches the financial base handoff exactly, that each business claim resolves to a named row of the business view handoff, that Management Language rows stay attributed, and that the two printed purchases figures (portfolio purchases by geography and the cash flow figure net of put-backs) are not mixed.
